subject: Meridian-13B: temporary ingress shim and staged freeze request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Meridian-13B: temporary ingress shim and staged freeze request

Team —

Novus (contact: Evan Price) ran a quick pre-prod run on Meridian-13B yesterday and flagged two issues that would block a full ingress:

- Tokenizer divergence: punctuation handling differs vs our tokenizer and we see ~1.8% end-user output regression on a small eval set.
- Quantization parity: model uses a custom 4-bit layout; runtime executes but KV cache size differs which breaks some cache reuse heuristics and spikes token latency on long contexts.

They need the model onboarded this quarter for a partner pilot; they asked if we can do a short-lived ingress shim (runtime-side adapter to normalize token IDs + KV pad) and a staged freeze (pin the served variant to v1.0-compat for 10 days) while we finalize a proper tokenizer mapping and quantization kernel.

Asking for two things from infra/product:
1) Permission to allow a provisional ingress shim in staging and a one-week production canary (p95 latency SLO to be enforced) — this would be accompanied by an automatic rollback if error rate or hallucination metric crosses thresholds.
2) Agreement on a pin window and explicit telemetry flags we need enabled (suggested flags in attached telemetry-coverage.csv).

I've attached the compatibility diff summary (meridian-compat-diff.pdf) and a minimal telemetry coverage checklist. If we can get alignment today I will tell Novus the expected timeline and coordinate their procurement.

Questions for Karthik: is the shim feasible without a model recompile?
For David: any objections on the proposed canary cadence/rollout windows from CS/ops?

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: meridian-compat-diff.pdf (summary), telemetry-coverage.csv (checklist)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Meridian-13B: temporary ingress shim and staged freeze request

Marissa —

Short answer: yes, a lightweight ingress shim is feasible without a full recompile, but caveats:

- Tokenizer mapping: we can implement a deterministic remap layer that translates Meridian token IDs to our canonical tokenizer on request ingress. This will avoid changing model weights. Latency impact should be ~+3–8ms per request in staging (needs verification).
- KV padding: we can pad/reslice KV cache to match our cache expectations. That is more delicate — it will work for short contexts but for >=4096 tokens we'll see cache thrash unless we cap the session length or force KV truncation.

Operational asks from my side:
1) We need a strict canary guard: start with 1% traffic, expand to 5% after 24h if p95 latency and noc errors are within thresholds.
2) Enable the following telemetry flags (short names): meridian.token_map, meridian.kv_pad, meridian.latency_probe. These should be present in the canary and collected at token granularity.
3) A rollback play: immediate auto-failover to the fallback variant (Meridian-13B-slim-v0) if hallucination AUC > baseline + 0.04 or token error rate > 0.75%.

I'll prepare a short patch for the shim this afternoon and push to staging. I recommend we mark the variant pinned to "v1.0-provisional" in the registry for the agreed freeze window so automated rollouts won't replace it.

Karthik
Lead, Inference Runtime

Marissa / Karthik —

From a CS/ops standpoint I have two items:

1) Procurement/contract: Novus asked for a 30-day pilot SLA (credits for downtime). Procurement (cc'd earlier in the chain) will need a clear risk disclosure. I can draft a one-paragraph risk addendum but we should avoid promising pinned windows longer than 14 days in writing.

2) Rollout schedule: ops can support the 1% -> 5% -> 20% expansion cadence but we need an explicit quiesce window (we prefer rollouts to happen during UTC 02:00–08:00). If Karthik's patch requires a maintenance window, please propose one. Also want post-mortem ownership clarified: who runs the incident if the shim causes cache thrash?

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik pushes shim to staging today (as suggested).
- Ops will run a 48 hour stability harness on the shim in staging with synthetic long-context traces.
- If stable, we do a 1% canary during UTC 03:00–05:00 next Mon, ramp after 24h.
- Procurement and I will approve a 14-day provisional pin; any extension requires exec sign-off.

David
Director, Customer Reliability

All —

Thanks for the quick triage. I approve the provisional plan with the following clarifications:

- Pin window: 14 days max (aligns with Procurement).
- Canary gates: p95 latency delta <= +20ms AND hallucination AUC delta <= +0.03. Both must pass to proceed to next ramp step.
- Telemetry: must include token-level meridian.latency_probe and the meridian.token_map histogram for sampling at 1/10k requests at minimum.

Marissa, please confirm you'll add the short risk addendum for Novus. Karthik, loop in SRE on the staging harness and attach the canary dashboard link in the Jira ticket (INF-4821).

Once those three items are in place, Ops can schedule the 1% canary window Monday UTC 03:00–04:00.

SG
